Simulated counts for the hab example

Source: R/data_files.R
count_data.Rd

Simulated counts at the 75 points in pts, for learning to estimate a scale of effect with the hab.tif raster.

Usage

data(count_data)

Format

A data frame with 75 rows, one per point in pts, and 2 columns:

  • y: integer count at each point.

  • hab: kernel-weighted mean of the binary hab.tif raster around each point, centered and scaled to unit variance.

Source

Simulated for this package.

Details

Counts were simulated from a Poisson distribution with an intercept of 0.5, a hab coefficient of 0.75 (log scale), and a Gaussian scale of effect (sigma) of 75 map units. A fit that recovers a sigma near 75 and a coefficient near 0.75 is working as intended.

See also

pts, hab, multiScale_optim().

Examples

data(count_data)
head(count_data)
#>   y        hab
#> 1 1 -0.7550406
#> 2 6  1.5678284
#> 3 0  0.3289698
#> 4 0 -0.6590483
#> 5 0 -0.5295792
#> 6 4  1.1883843
# Starting model: hab will be replaced by values at each candidate scale
glm(y ~ hab, family = poisson, data = count_data)
#> 
#> Call:  glm(formula = y ~ hab, family = poisson, data = count_data)
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)          hab  
#>      0.4802       0.8705  
#> 
#> Degrees of Freedom: 74 Total (i.e. Null);  73 Residual
#> Null Deviance:	    186.6 
#> Residual Deviance: 70.24 	AIC: 232.3
